goal: Design (not implement) two independent, optional, default-off integrations between msfslogger and SayIntentions.AI's pilot-facing SAPI: (1) pull — import SayIntentions' getCommsHistory ATC/CPDLC transcript into a flight's existing acars_messages thread; (2) push — send msfslogger's already-generated PDC/clearance content into the pilot's live SayIntentions session via sayAs(channel=ACARS_IN), condensed to fit the 128-character cap. This run stops after Design: the task graph below is the full plan a future run executes, but only T-001/T-002 (Design + its review) run in this session.
frozen_decisions: "I don't have a partner API. Narrow it down to what can be integrated with a pilot's api." — scope is pilot-key (api_key) endpoints only; importVAData and any partner va_api_key-gated endpoint is out of scope entirely.

"yes, write the specification for both designs. It's fine to have an extra per-flight step of linking the two sessions, as sayintentions can't be assumed for regular usage of msfslogger and is an optional enhancement option." — a manual per-flight (or per-trip) linking step is an accepted, frozen part of the design, not a gap to design around.
Both features are fully optional/default-off: an operator who never sets a SayIntentions key sees zero behavior change anywhere else in the app.
Reuse the existing acars_messages table for both directions unless a concrete reason rules it out for one of them — if so, that reason is stated explicitly in the design, not assumed.

setFreq/setVar/setPause/getAirport/assignGate/getParking/getWX/getVATSIM/getTFRs/importVAData are out of scope for this run (per intake.md's out-of-scope list) — the design must not grow the surface to cover them.
sequencing_rationale: Design is its own gated phase (T-001 + its reviewer T-002) because both directions share one settings key, one HTTP client and one message-storage decision — freezing that contract before any code exists is what keeps the four implementation phases from redoing it independently, per CLAUDE.md's 'freeze it before any code is written.'

Foundation (phase 2: settings storage, the SayIntentions HTTP client, the migration decision) ships before either feature because both pull and push need a stored, validated API key and a working, independently-testable client (src/inspect-sayintentions.ts) to build on — proving connectivity in isolation before either feature's business logic sits on top of it.

Pull ships before push (phase 3 before phase 4) because getCommsHistory has no active-session requirement and no in-sim side effect — it is the lower-risk half, and it establishes the flight-linking UI/endpoint pattern that push's confirmation UI reuses.

Push ships last (phase 4) because it carries the run's highest risk: the 128-char ACARS_IN condensation of ClearanceDetails, the no-active-session failure mode, and an irreversible in-sim side effect (sayAs is fire-and-forget, unlike a local database write). It benefits from the error-handling and client groundwork phase 3 already proved.

Within a phase, the backend and frontend tasks depend only on the previous phase's reviewer gate, not on each other: both code against the design frozen in T-001, and the frontend verifies itself with mockFetch/renderWithProviders (client/src/test/*) rather than a live backend, so the two can run in parallel — their allowed_paths (src/**+tests/** vs client/**) are disjoint.

Every phase's reviewer task gates the next phase's first task. That is also what makes it safe for client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx to be edited in both phase 3 (T-007) and phase 4 (T-010), and for src/routes/sayIntentions.ts to be edited in both phase 3 (T-006) and phase 4 (T-009): the two edits are always serialized by a review gate, never concurrent.

No devops/ship phase: neither direction adds a new npm dependency (both use Node 20's built-in fetch, same as src/weatherClient.ts) or touches build/packaging/deploy. Per the loop, Ship is skipped when a run doesn't touch those — recorded here rather than added as a no-op phase.

phases.name: Design
phases.ships: A frozen design.md: exact settings/link storage (with an explicit migration-or-reuse decision), the sayIntentionsClient.ts contract, the full REST surface for pull and push, the condensed-message algorithm with worked examples, and every failure mode mapped to a status/error code — reviewed and approved before any implementation code exists.

phases.name: Foundation: API key setting + SayIntentions HTTP client
phases.ships: An operator can save, view (masked) and clear a SayIntentions pilot API key from the app, mirroring the existing SimBrief-key field exactly; a CLI inspector and a hermetic Vitest suite prove getCommsHistory/sayAs connectivity and error-mapping without going through the app. No other route's behavior changes.

phases.name: Pull: import SayIntentions comms into the ACARS thread
phases.ships: From a flight's ACARS page, an operator with a saved key can link the flight to their current SayIntentions session and import its comms transcript into that flight's ACARS thread, incrementally and without duplicate rows on repeated imports.

phases.name: Push: send the PDC/clearance into the live SayIntentions session
phases.ships: From a flight's ACARS page, once a clearance has been requested, an operator can send a condensed version of it to their live SayIntentions session as a real in-sim ACARS_IN message, with a clear, non-crashing outcome when no SayIntentions session is currently active.

tasks.title: Freeze the SayIntentions pull+push contract: settings/link storage, migration decision, client contract, condensed-message algorithm, REST surface, failure-mode table
tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-17-sayintentions-integration/design.md covering both directions end to end, so every implementation task below (T-003 through T-010) can be executed from this document alone, cold, without re-deriving any of these decisions.
acceptance_criteria: design.md uses top-level (##) headings containing, case-insensitively, at least these keywords so ctx.sh design <run-id> <keyword> can slice them: 'settings' (API key storage), 'link' (session-correlation storage), 'migration' (the schema decision), 'client' (sayIntentionsClient.ts contract), 'pull', 'push', 'condensed' (the ACARS_IN message algorithm), 'failure' (the error-mode table), 'trigger' (button vs poll), 'ingest' (MCDU/x-ingest-token scope), 'frontend' (client contract), 'contracts' (a per-task frozen-contracts section addressed to T-003/T-004/T-006/T-007/T-009/T-010 by id).

Settings section states the exact new app_setting key name for the pilot API key (mirroring SIMBRIEF_USER_ID_SETTING, reusing getSetting/setSetting from src/db/settings.ts verbatim, no new table) and the exact validation rule for a well-formed key (or states there is none beyond non-empty, per SayIntentions publishing no documented key format).

Link section states, for the per-flight-or-trip session-link value: the exact storage mechanism (a composite app_setting key such as sayintentions_link:<flight_id>, or a new table) and, concretely, what it holds (at minimum: linked-at timestamp; for pull, the last-imported since_id cursor). It states which scope is linkable — flight, planned leg, or both — and why, by analogy to the existing scoping of wx (both) versus loadsheet/clearance (planned-leg only) in src/routes/acars.ts.

Migration section gives an explicit yes/no: if a new table or column is required, it gives full CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE DDL in the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN idiom already used in src/db/schema.ts, states the ON DELETE behavior when the linked flight or planned leg is deleted (PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON is active), and names the new src/db/*.ts file it lives in, mirroring src/db/acarsMessages.ts. If no migration is needed (composite app_setting keys suffice), it says so and states why that scales fine at msfslogger's data volumes (a handful of settings rows, not a queryable index).

Client section declares sayIntentionsClient.ts's exported functions with full signatures: getCommsHistory(apiKey: string, sinceId?: number) and sayAs(apiKey: string, params: {...}), a SayIntentionsFetchError class mirroring WeatherFetchError's shape (code, message, userMessage, optional httpStatus), and a closed SayIntentionsErrorCode union covering at minimum NO_KEY, NETWORK, TIMEOUT, BAD_STATUS, BAD_BODY and a sayAs-only NO_ACTIVE_SESSION — with the exact HTTP-status/body heuristic used to detect NO_ACTIVE_SESSION, since the docs only say the call is 'expected to fail' with no documented code.

Pull section specifies the exact route(s) (method, path, request body if any, success response shape, status codes), the exact category/label/dedup_key used when filing each imported comm_history row into acars_messages (dedup_key formula must incorporate SayIntentions' own comm_history[].id, e.g. sayintentions:comm:<id>, so a repeat pull is a no-op via insertAcarsMessageOnce), the exact mapping from comm_history[] fields (listed in sayintentions-api-notes.md) to { direction, label, body }, and confirms acars_messages is reused as-is for this direction or states the concrete reason it cannot be.

Push section specifies the exact route (leg-scoped, flight-scoped, or both — justified against the clearance route's existing leg-only scoping in src/routes/acars.ts), how it locates the flight/leg's already-generated ClearanceDetails (parsing the existing pdc/uplink acars_messages row's payload_json, the same way parseDispatchPayload does today), the exact success/failure response shapes and status codes (including 404/409 when no clearance has been requested yet, and the sayAs NO_ACTIVE_SESSION mapping), and confirms whether a successful push is recorded as a new acars_messages row (state its category/label/direction/dedup_key) or as an update to the existing pdc row's payload_json — with a reason either way.

Condensed-message section gives the exact template and field order built from ClearanceDetails { departure_icao, destination_icao, route, initial_altitude_ft, squawk }, states the truncation/priority rule applied when the already-clamped route (src/acars.ts's clampRoute) still doesn't fit under 128 characters, and gives at least 3 worked examples with the exact rendered string and its character count: a short route, a route long enough to require truncation, and a clearance with route === null.

Trigger section states, separately for pull and for push, whether it is operator-initiated (a button) or a background poll, with a one-paragraph rationale each, consistent with the frozen decision that a manual per-flight linking step is accepted rather than something to engineer around.
Ingest section states explicitly whether any new route is added to src/auth/ingestScope.ts's INGEST_SCOPED_ROUTES allow-list for the MCDU client, and why or why not, for each new route individually.

Failure-mode section is a table with one row per: no API key set, no session link established, no active SayIntentions session (push only), upstream network/timeout error, upstream non-200 status, malformed/unparseable upstream JSON body — each row naming the HTTP status, the { error, code } shape returned, and confirming none of these ever produces an unhandled exception (500 is reserved for genuinely unexpected failures, same posture as the existing wx route in src/routes/acars.ts).

Default-off section states exactly what getSetting(<the new setting key>) === null causes at every new route (e.g. 409 with a NO_API_KEY code) and confirms, by name, that no existing route, response shape or UI element changes when the key has never been set.

The per-task frozen-contracts section gives, for each of T-003, T-004, T-006, T-007, T-009, T-010 below, the exact interfaces/DDL/route paths/response shapes that task must implement verbatim — same style as the worked example in .claude/runs/2026-09-04-lnmpln-trip-planner/plan.json's T-002 frozen_contracts field (readable via ctx.sh task 2026-09-04-lnmpln-trip-planner T-002).

design.md contains no implementation code beyond type/interface stubs and DDL, and does not reintroduce any item from intake.md's out-of-scope list (importVAData, setFreq/setVar/setPause/getAirport/assignGate/getParking, getWX/getVATSIM/getTFRs).
